note: Additional CIS SQL Server checks loaded via the bulk-import pipeline.

checks.title: 'user options' is 0
checks.query: SELECT CAST(value_in_use AS INT) v FROM sys.configurations WHERE name='user options'

checks.title: 'Database Mail XPs' is disabled
checks.query: SELECT CAST(value_in_use AS INT) v FROM sys.configurations WHERE name='Database Mail XPs'
checks.remediation: EXEC sp_configure 'Database Mail XPs',0; RECONFIGURE; (unless DB Mail is used).

checks.title: 'clr strict security' is enabled
checks.query: SELECT CAST(value_in_use AS INT) v FROM sys.configurations WHERE name='clr strict security'

checks.title: The 'sa' login has been renamed
checks.query: SELECT name FROM sys.server_principals WHERE principal_id=1
checks.remediation: ALTER LOGIN [sa] WITH NAME=[<newname>]; — rename the well-known sa account.

checks.title: CONTROL SERVER not granted to logins other than sysadmins
checks.query: SELECT p.name FROM sys.server_permissions sp JOIN sys.server_principals p ON p.principal_id=sp.grantee_principal_id WHERE sp.permission_name='CONTROL SERVER' AND sp.state IN ('G','W') AND p.name NOT LIKE '##%'
checks.remediation: REVOKE CONTROL SERVER FROM [<login>]; — it is equivalent to sysadmin.

checks.title: securityadmin role membership limited
checks.query: SELECT p.name FROM sys.server_role_members m JOIN sys.server_principals p ON p.principal_id=m.member_principal_id JOIN sys.server_principals r ON r.principal_id=m.role_principal_id WHERE r.name='securityadmin' AND p.name NOT LIKE '##%'
checks.remediation: ALTER SERVER ROLE securityadmin DROP MEMBER [<login>]; — it can grant any permission.

checks.title: A SQL Server Audit is enabled
checks.query: SELECT name FROM sys.server_audits WHERE is_state_enabled=1
checks.remediation: Create + enable a Server Audit (login success/failure, permission changes) per CIS §5.
